purpose: Determine before each new municipality batch whether a municipality can be researched inside a normal batch or should be handled as a standalone deep-dive. Population alone is not decisive; legal/product complexity is the primary criterion.

housingRegulationBreadth.0: no specific municipal housing regime found in intake
housingRegulationBreadth.3: four or more distinct regimes, e.g. room rental, splitting, purchase protection, tourist/short stay, rental permit

geographicComplexity.2: multiple districts, maps, thresholds or area-specific rules
geographicComplexity.3: multiple maps/geometry layers, postcode/address lists or overlapping geographic regimes

applicationComplexity.0: single Omgevingsloket route with dynamic documents
applicationComplexity.3: multiple separate products with distinct document sets, fees, exceptions and processing rules

legalSourceComplexity.3: transitional law, recent amendments, overlapping old/new instruments or conflicting current-looking pages

specialComplexitySignals.1_each_up_to_3: Bibob-specific matrix; heritage/monument overlay; labour-migrant regime; student/target-group regime; vacation/short-stay regime; recent major 2026 transition; extensive annex/geometry dependency

classification.5-7: heavy-batch: include only if batch contains at most one municipality in this class

overrideRules: Any municipality with three or more distinct geographic housing regimes is standalone regardless of population.
Any municipality with a recent transition regime plus multiple separate housing permit products is standalone.
If the initial pass already produces more than three unresolved article/form matrices, handle standalone.
A large population by itself never forces standalone treatment if the legal regime is simple.
A small municipality can still be standalone if the legal/product structure is unusually complex.
